built_to: the letter of draft-xg-payment-dispute-profile-02 as we read it (letter.READINGS); not a claim of conformance

checks: receipt signature verified over the canonical payload bytes with the key resolved out of band (3, 4)
the receipt carries the eleven profile members of Section 4
signer_pubkey_hash is the SHA-256 of the raw Ed25519 public key bytes of the key resolved (5)
settlement anchor_hash recomputed over the anchor object inside the anchored block (5, 8.3)
settlement amount and currency equal the manifest's headline amount (9: headline consistency)
6 ledger events recompute and link (9)
ledger_entry_hash is the ActionExecuted event of this action; its action_packet_hash equals action_hash (5)
scope verdict re-derived from the intent scope and executed action the ScopeEvaluated event records: in_scope; receipt and manifest headline agree (8.2, 9)
action_hash is the canonical hash of the executed_action recorded in the ScopeEvaluated event (5)
3 custody events each name a ledger event hash of the slice (8.4: a binding, not an authentication)

times.note: 11: the receipt's timestamp is claimed by its producer and is not trusted time; no Transparency Service Receipt is among this verifier's inputs, so no registration time is reported

rail_anchors_hash.construction: this module's reading, not the text's: equal to the settlement anchor_hash

evidence_set_hash.construction: this module's, not the text's: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the sorted digests the packet cites

anchors.name: allow_outcome_receipt
anchors.state: not resolved: verifier holds nothing of that type

anchors.name: tool_result_receipt
anchors.state: not resolved: verifier holds nothing of that type

anchors.name: approval_event_hash
anchors.state: resolved in the ledger slice: the event's action_hash is the receipt's

re_derived.fre901: 8.4: the acquisition, custody and authentication records are the producer's claims, not covered by the receipt signature or the ledger chain; this verifier checked their shape and the custody bindings and does not report them as authenticated

checks: the receipt payload has the eleven members of Section 4 and no other
every value of the receipt payload is a string, a boolean or null (4)
the manifest names draft-xg-payment-dispute-profile-02
the manifest carries receipt_public_key_hex, whose SHA-256 is the receipt's signer_pubkey_hash (4, 5); a hint, not a key resolved out of band
approval_event_hash is an ApprovalGranted or ApprovalDenied event of the slice whose payload carries the receipt's action_hash (5)
the approval event points to no approval held outside the ledger (5)
the statement's payload is, byte for byte, the canonical bytes of the packet's receipt envelope (6, reading R1)
the statement's signature verifies, under alg -19, with the receipt key resolved out of band (6: "signed with the receipt's own signing key")
the statement's kid is the receipt's key_id, as a byte string (reading R4)
the CWT claims carry an issuer (6)
the subject is the action identifier of the packet manifest (6)

R1 the payload of the Signed Statement.text: 6: "The Signed Statement is a COSE_Sign1 [RFC9052] whose payload is the receipt's canonical bytes"; 3: a dispute receipt is "an Ed25519 ([RFC8032]) signature over an [RFC8785] (JCS) canonicalized payload, in an envelope of the form {payload, signature{alg, kid, sig}}"
R1 the payload of the Signed Statement.open: the receipt's canonical bytes can be the canonical bytes of the whole envelope, or of its payload member alone
R1 the payload of the Signed Statement.choice: the JCS bytes of the whole envelope {payload, signature}: the receipt is the envelope (Section 3), and Appendix A gives SHA-256(R) and a leaf hash for the envelope R, which is printed in that form. The receipt's own signature is then inside the registered bytes

R2 the COSE algorithm identifier.text: 6: "signed with the receipt's own signing key"; 4: "Signature: Ed25519, lowercase hex (alg = EdDSA)"
R2 the COSE algorithm identifier.open: the COSE_Sign1 needs an integer alg; Ed25519 has two, -8 (EdDSA, RFC 9053) and -19 (Ed25519, RFC 9864); the text names neither
R2 the COSE algorithm identifier.choice: -19, the identifier ts.isoluce.net signs its receipts with and the one the statements of ../registration carry; check_statement accepts -8 as well

R3 the content type.text: 6: the bullet that describes the Signed Statement names its payload, its key, the CWT claims issuer and subject
R3 the content type.open: no content type (COSE header 3) is named
R3 the content type.choice: application/json, as the statements of ../registration carry for a JSON payload

R4 the kid of the Signed Statement.text: 6: "A party that already trusts the receipt key needs no other key to check the statement"; 5: "key_id names that key in the operator's published keyring"
R4 the kid of the Signed Statement.open: the text does not say how the COSE_Sign1 names the key; RFC 9943 Section 6 requires a kid when there is no x5t or x5chain
R4 the kid of the Signed Statement.choice: the receipt's key_id, as a byte string (ts.isoluce.net refuses a kid that is not a byte string)

R5 the issuer.text: 6: "with the CWT claims issuer set to an identifier the registering party supplies (the receipt payload carries none)"
R5 the issuer.choice: urn:example:merchant:dispute-desk, the fictional desk the packet's acquisition record names: the key is a test key whose seed is public, so the statement is put under no real identifier

R6 the eleven members and approval_event.text: 4: "Payload: the implementation's PolicyDecisionReceipt canonical dict -- decision, reason_code, action_hash, evidence_set_hash, ledger_entry_hash, timestamp, mandate_hash, rail_anchors_hash, scope_conformance, key_id, signer_pubkey_hash"; 5: "the receipt fields that bind to other parts of the packet are built as follows", a list that includes approval_event_hash and anchor_hash; 8.2: the agent_anchors block carries the "approval event hash"
R6 the eleven members and approval_event.open: whether approval_event_hash and anchor_hash are members of the receipt payload
R6 the eleven members and approval_event.choice: no: the payload has the eleven members of Section 4 and no other, as the vector of Appendix A does; approval_event_hash is in the manifest's agent_anchors block (8.2), anchor_hash in its settlement block (8.3)

R7 mandate_hash without an AP2 mandate.text: 8.2: "AP2 mandate_hash"; "Network token id and 3DS/ACS result are part of the block's shape but null when the implementation has no source for them"; 4: "the receipt dict is strings, booleans, null"
R7 mandate_hash without an AP2 mandate.open: whether mandate_hash may be null when the approval is a person's and not an AP2 mandate
R7 mandate_hash without an AP2 mandate.choice: null, in the receipt and in the agent_anchors block

R8 evidence_set_hash and rail_anchors_ha.text: 5: "evidence_set_hash and rail_anchors_hash are signed but not re-derived by the reference verifier in this revision; a verifier MUST NOT report them as checked"
R8 evidence_set_hash and rail_anchors_ha.open: what the two values are built from
R8 evidence_set_hash and rail_anchors_ha.choice: the constructions of the parent case (the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the sorted digests the packet cites; the settlement anchor_hash). They are signed and not reported as checked

R9 the manifest, the ledger slice and th.text: Appendix B: "The packet manifest, the ledger slice and the ledger event hash are named but not yet defined in this document"
R9 the manifest, the ledger slice and th.choice: the shapes of the parent case, which ../goshi_from_text.py reads; a member profile in the manifest names the revision the packet was built to (the text asks for no such member)

R10 a number in the recorded action.text: 5: "action_hash: the canonical hash of the executed-action object recorded in the action's ScopeEvaluated ledger event"; "'Canonical hash' means lowercase hex SHA-256 over the canonical bytes of Section 4"; 4: "the receipt dict is strings, booleans, null, and nested objects/arrays of the same, with amounts pre-converted to decimal strings before canonicalization"
R10 a number in the recorded action.open: whether the value domain stated for the receipt dict also binds the recorded executed-action and intent-scope objects
R10 a number in the recorded action.choice: no: the two recorded objects keep amount_minor as the integer the tool door saw (12000), which JCS writes as a plain integer, so that action_hash is the digest the other three links of the chain carry. The receipt itself holds strings and null only
